Response LBNL Report #2001653 was variable, though it was possible to assemble teams of 3-6 individuals for interviews, for each topical area comprising different laboratories. At the conclusion of the interviews, the interviewees were asked for suggestions of similar researchers in other laboratories, and the process was repeated with them. Our interviews covered the three weapons laboratories, as well as Y12, LBNL, Pacific Northwest National Laboratory, Idaho National Laboratory, Savannah River National Laboratory, and ORNL. National Laboratory employees that are former IAEA inspectors and team leads for the Nuclear Compliance Verification (NCV), Federal employees in NER and NER teams’ active members were also interviewed. 3.2 Conducting interviews The interviews were conducted either in person or over computer-based videoconferencing (Zoom, Teams etc.). Each interview was prefaced with a presentation that described the technology, the real-world use-cases on which it had been tried, a movie of a drone-mounted SDF in action (include source reconstruction visualized on a tablet), and a bibliography. Having illustrated what SDF could accomplish (and explained the sensors and algorithms that enable the capabilities), the interviewees were asked to (1) speculate about the use-cases in their field of investigation for which the SDF capability could be re-purposed, (2) any necessary expansion of the sensor suite that would be required to do so, (3) the additional sensing modalities that might be required or helpful, e.g., neutron sensing, (4) additions in path planning and movement control that may facilitate autonomous system use, and (5) enhancements required in the source reconstruction software (e.g., model selection between different types of sources, fusion of measurement modalities of different types, incorporation of shielding etc.). The interviews were interactive - the project team learned about new use-cases as the interviewees learned about SDF. Some interviews resulted in deep discussions, spread over multiple sessions. Post-interview, the proceedings were summarized with a view of (1) capturing a new use-case of SDF and (2) the capability enhancements (sensors, reconstruction algorithms, and path planning & control) that would be needed. 3.3 2023 Radiological Data Fusion Workshop Afterinterviewingexperts,LBNLandSNLorganizedaRadiologicalDataFusionWorkshop,heldat LBNL August 15-16, 2023. Over 100 researchers, federal sponsors and practitioners of nuclear non- proliferation, radiological security, and other missions related to the NNSA were directly invited to the workshop and several others received an invitation through forwarding by invitees. The hybrid workshop comprised 30 in-person participants and another approximately 20 participating online. Representatives from seven national laboratories, including both researchers and practitioners were present, as were federal representatives from NA-22, NA-80, NA-24, NA- 21, DTRA, DHS S&T, UK AWE and the UK Home Office.
